sqlite_primary_source.source: SQLite official PRAGMA documentation, PRAGMA data_version
observed_semantics: Two data_version reads on the same connection differ when any other connection commits changes to the database in between.
Commits made on the same connection do not change that connection's data_version value.
data_version is connection-local and values from different connections must not be compared as database identity.

serious_counterhypothesis.statement: A connection-local PRAGMA main.data_version fence is database-wide rather than WP206-table-specific. If canonical UnifiedDB legitimately permits other components/connections to commit unrelated tables while CanonicalPersistentAgencyStore remains open, the proposed hard fence will classify those legitimate commits as UNIFIEDDB_EXTERNAL_SQLITE_REVISION_DRIFT and can make the long-lived agency store unusable under normal multi-writer operation.
serious_counterhypothesis.why_material: UnifiedDB is one canonical authority substrate intended to host multiple typed tables/readers/writers. Detecting every other-connection commit is stronger than detecting unauthorized mutation of WP206-owned state.
cheapest_discriminator: Open CanonicalPersistentAgencyStore on a fixture UnifiedDB and establish the G6 data_version baseline.
From a second legitimate connection, commit only to a non-WP206 table that is explicitly outside CHECKPOINT_TABLE/recovery ownership.
Call the canonical WP206 read/write identity guard on the original store.
If the guard raises UNIFIEDDB_EXTERNAL_SQLITE_REVISION_DRIFT, record that G6 is a database-wide concurrency fence, not a WP206-state revision fence.
Then either prove the runtime contract intentionally grants WP206 an exclusive/single-writer database epoch, or narrow the fence to an owned-state revision witness before acceptance.
serious_counterhypothesis.acceptance_rule: Do not reconcile G6 merely because hostile external DML/DDL is detected. Acceptance also requires a declared and tested answer for legitimate unrelated UnifiedDB commits; otherwise the mechanism may close one stale-state gap by breaking the shared canonical substrate contract.
